rationale: Banned tolokers are defined by work behaviour (approval and rejection statistics inside the 10 profile/performance features), not by where they sit in the co-participation graph: an edge only means 'shared a task', so at avg_degree 88.28, density 0.015017 and clustering_coeff 0.5329 every worker, banned or not, sits inside a dense project pool. That kills the structure-rarity views. The 26 communities at modularity 0.5194 essentially recover the 13 projects, so community non-adherence measures which project a worker joined rather than whether they were banned; spectral has the weakest landmarker tail (p95 0.4157) because high-frequency signal smears across degree-88 neighbourhoods; and density is dead on arrival (p50 = p90 = p95 = 0.0), consistent with is_power_law = false, meaning there is no rare structural fringe for LOF/kNN to isolate. Bans are a platform policy outcome, a sizeable class rather than a handful of outliers, which is precisely the regime where rarity-based scoring collapses and a global normal boundary still rank-orders usefully. Hence one_class first: with feature_dim 10 and feature_sparsity 0.4803 the attribute space is low-dimensional and dense, so an SVDD envelope around the bulk performance profile is well posed, and distance from the centre is the direct reading of 'this worker's statistics fall outside what the platform tolerates'. attr_struct_mismatch is second on its own evidence, the widest and best extended upper tail of any landmarker (std 0.2454, p90 0.7175, p99 0.9141), and it is orthogonal to a global boundary: it flags workers whose performance attributes disagree with the standing their co-participation gives them, someone embedded in normal task pools whose numbers do not match the crowd they work beside. reconstruction supplies a third, generative view (DOMINANT reconstructs attributes and structure jointly), catching workers whose feature vector cannot be predicted from their neighbourhood at all; 10 feature dimensions train cleanly. Rejected though applicable: conformity is saturated rather than separated (p50 0.8696 exceeds every other paradigm's p90, and p90 0.9357 to p99 0.9686 is a compressed ceiling), so it calls nearly everyone conformant and carries little ranking information, with feature_dup_rate 0.489 only marginally over its 0.4 trigger. local_affinity and homophily_violation are both neighbour-agreement views that concentrate toward the global mean at avg_degree 88, and homophily 0.7492 already says neighbours agree, so they would duplicate the reconstruction view on less spread (p99 0.6969 and 0.8410).

A Toloka ban is a verdict about the worker, not about the worker's neighborhood: it is issued from profile and task-performance statistics, which are exactly the node attributes here (feature_dim = 10). The positive class therefore lives in a global region of attribute space (low approval, atypical throughput, short tenure), not in a local inconsistency, and one_class is the only paradigm whose assumption states that directly: distance from a learned normal boundary in embedding space. The edge semantics argue against the neighborhood paradigms. An edge means 'worked on the same task', so a banned worker's neighbors are overwhelmingly ordinary workers who happened to share a project; with avg_degree = 88.28, density = 0.0150 and clustering_coeff = 0.5329 every node sits inside a dense co-participation blob, and homophily = 0.7492 is measured over activity-level features that encode which projects a worker did, not ban status. The landmarkers confirm it: local_affinity has no separated tail (mean 0.2295, p95 0.4959), and community is similarly gradual (mean 0.2552, p95 0.5989), so local_affinity, homophily_violation, contrastive and community would all be redundant re-readings of the same weak neighborhood agreement signal. reconstruction is kept as the complementary global-attribute view: on a dense, high-homophily graph neighborhood-smoothed feature reconstruction is well conditioned, and its residual surface (what the worker's shared-task context fails to predict about their statistics) is a different error geometry from SVDD distance to a center, so the two disagree on informative nodes rather than duplicating. attr_struct_mismatch is the only landmarker with a genuinely separated upper tail (std 0.2454, p90 0.7175, p95 0.7991, p99 0.9141) and it is cross-modal by construction: it flags workers whose quality attributes disagree with their co-participation footprint, the signature of a high-volume toloker whose output quality does not match their activity (degree_std = 161.82, max_degree = 2138). Two paradigms are explicitly rejected despite passing their applicability gates. density is degenerate on this graph: p50 = p90 = p95 = 0.0 with mean 0.0023, because kNN distances collapse at avg_degree 88 in a 10-dimensional space with feature_dup_rate 0.489, so it carries almost no ranking information. conformity is a false trigger: the dup_rate = 0.489 that enables it comes from a 10-dim, 48 percent sparse statistics matrix where collisions are arithmetic rather than from templated fake profiles, and its distribution is saturated and left-skewed (mean 0.8111 with p50 0.8696 above the mean, p99 only 0.9686), i.e. a compressed ceiling with no separated upper tail. Banned tolokers are banned for performance that the platform recorded, they are not camouflaged actors hiding behind minimal profiles, so the camouflage-by-conformity mechanism it assumes is not the mechanism that produces this label.

The domain fixes what a positive is: a worker banned by a project for how they behaved, and the 10 node features are exactly profile plus task-performance statistics, i.e. the same evidence a project uses to ban. So the target is a worker whose performance envelope sits outside the normal worker envelope, which is the one_class assumption read literally. I put it first. Note that the sibling global view, density, is unusable here: its landmarker is degenerate (p50 = p90 = p95 = 0.0, mean 0.0023), so local kNN/LOF density estimates collapse in this embedding and the boundary has to be learned globally (SVDD) rather than estimated locally. That is a reason to prefer one_class over density, not a reason to drop the global view. Second, attr_struct_mismatch: edges mean 'worked on the same task', so structural position encodes how much and how broadly a worker participates, not whether they cheat. A banned worker is typically structurally ordinary or even prolific (avg_degree 88.28, max_degree 2138, clustering_coeff 0.5329, so participation is dense and unremarkable for most) while being attributively deviant. That attribute/structure disagreement is the ban signature, and this paradigm has by far the best separated tail in the landmarkers (p50 0.3138 to p95 0.7991 to p99 0.9141, std 0.2454). Third, homophily_violation adds a peer-conditioned view that the other two lack: with homophily 0.7492 and avg_degree 88.28, a worker's neighbors are the other workers on the same tasks, so the neighborhood mean is a stable estimate of the expected performance profile for that task mix. Deviating from it flags bad performance relative to task peers, which is closer to a ban decision than raw global oddity (a globally unusual but elite worker is not banned). Its tail is the second widest (p50 0.3628 to p99 0.8410). Rejected: conformity, despite feature_dup_rate 0.4890 clearing its gate, because its distribution is saturated rather than separated (mean 0.8111, p50 0.8696, p99 0.9686, so nearly every node reads as conformant and the tail carries little information), and because the camouflage story does not fit this domain: bans are decided from the very performance statistics that make up the feature matrix, so anomalies should be feature-space outliers, not in-liers. The high dup rate is better explained mechanically by feature_dim 10 with feature_sparsity 0.4803, i.e. many workers sharing zero-valued rejected/skipped counters. Rejected community and spectral because the co-participation structure reflects project assignment (num_communities 26, modularity 0.5194 track the 13 projects and their task clusters), not ban status, and both have compressed tails (spectral p99 0.5512). Rejected local_affinity as redundant with homophily_violation, and rejected reconstruction because at homophily 0.7492 with 88-degree neighborhoods an autoencoder smooths to the neighborhood mean, making its residual a noisier copy of the same peer-conditioned signal. Rejected contrastive and adversarial: subgraph view agreement is dominated by sampling at this density (0.015017, ~1.04M edges) and GAN training is unstable at feature_dim 10.
